newsitem.title: PANAMA: Taiwan envoy to visit Panama to strengthen ties.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan envoy to visit Panama to strengthen ties.

text.p: Taiwan's Foreign Minister John Chang will meet with top Panamanian officials on Friday as the two nations seek to firm up ties after the Hong Kong handover to China, the Foreign Ministry said on Wednesday.
"He will meet the foreign minister and then the president on Friday," Foreign Ministry spokesman Eric Rodriguez Auerbach told Reuters.

Chang, who will visit 11 Central American and Caribbean nations, told reporters before his departure that he would exchange views with his counterpart on post-handover Hong Kong and explain Taipei's policies toward Beijing during his 22-day tour.

Panama's foreign minister, Ricardo Alberto Arias, said earlier this week that his country's diplomatic and commercial relations with Taiwan would not change because of the handover of Hong Kong to communist China.
But there is concern that this relationship could come under pressure as China forces the few nations with formal diplomatic links with Taiwan to downgrade or close their Hong Kong consulates.

Hong Kong is one of the most important users of the Panama Canal and the Colon free-trade zone -- the world's second largest after Hong Kong -- as a transit point for goods to other Latin American countries.
But Taiwan is also an important investor in Panama. Shipping giant Evergreen Marine has spent $200 million on a new port facility and has applied to set up its EVA Airways unit there.

The Taiwanese government has contributed $800,000 to help organise an international conference on the future of the Panama canal in September and its president, Lee Teng-hui, has said he will attend the conference.
